search_question: Is there a single causal skin experimental arm in which a mature/established fibrotic scar is directly documented before delayed intervention and the same scar subsequently shows endogenous de novo appendage regeneration rather than mere preservation, imported follicle tissue, or cross-arm inference?

retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.note: These criteria formalize the user-specified target after candidate discovery in this pass. This record does not claim prospective blindness or novelty prediction.
retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.S1: Mature or explicitly established fibrotic scar is directly documented before intervention in the same arm.
retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.S2: Intervention begins only after that documented state.
retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.S3: The intervention causally changes the scar/fibrotic remodeling outcome.
retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.S4: The treated scar demonstrates endogenous de novo appendage regeneration/neogenesis; preservation of pre-existing follicles, histological reappearance without lineage/neogenesis evidence, or transplantation of existing appendage tissue is insufficient for strict S4.
retrospective_gate_for_this_pass.S5: All qualifying evidence belongs to the same experimental arm; no species/arm fusion is allowed.

candidates.title: Locked nucleic acid-modified antisense oligonucleotides attenuate scar hyperplasia through targeted inhibition of CTGF
candidates.timeline: wounds healed at day 14; intralesional treatment began day 14; endpoint day 42
candidates.observed: scar area decreased; CTGF/collagen-I/collagen-III/alpha-SMA and profibrotic signaling decreased; new hair growth reported; histology after treatment showed reappearance of hair follicles and sebaceous glands
candidates.why_not: Healed wound at day 14 is not equivalent to an explicitly mature scar, and histological reappearance/new hair growth does not by itself establish endogenous de novo appendage neogenesis.

candidates.timeline: prominent raised firm reddish hypertrophic scars documented by day 28 with abnormal histology; four weeks of treatment followed
candidates.observed: scar protrusion and dermal thickness decreased; collagen became more organized; fibrosis markers decreased
candidates.why_not: The strong established-scar timing exists in the rabbit arm, but appendage regeneration was not established there. The mouse appendage observation cannot be fused into the rabbit arm.

candidates.title: Hedgehog stimulates hair follicle neogenesis by creating inductive dermis during murine skin wound healing
candidates.timeline: one delayed arm begins doxycycline at approximately post-wound day 10 plus/minus 2 days following re-epithelialization and continues to day 46
candidates.observed: new dermal papillae and neogenic hair follicles formed after wound closure, including differentiated follicular structures
candidates.why_not: The intervention is delayed until wound closure but not until a directly demonstrated mature fibrotic scar.

candidates.title: Transcriptome-guided development of a fibrosis-reversal compound reduces skin scarring and allows regeneration via mitochondrial uncoupling
candidates.timeline: FR-1 treatment begins 13 days post-injury after epithelialization, described as established scar during active remodeling/fibrotic phase
candidates.observed: scar area decreases; profibrotic myofibroblast phenotype and ECM are reduced; hair-follicle damage is avoided
candidates.why_not: Active remodeling/post-epithelialization is not the strict mature-scar state, and follicle preservation is not de novo appendage neogenesis.

candidates.title: Anagen hair follicles transplanted into mature human scars remodel fibrotic tissue
candidates.timeline: scars at least four years old; baseline biopsy before autologous anagen-hair-follicle transplantation; follow-up at 2, 4 and 6 months
candidates.observed: mature scar collagen, epidermis, vascularity and transcriptional state shift toward healthier skin
candidates.why_not: The intervention imports existing anagen hair follicles; it demonstrates mature scar remodelability, not endogenous de novo appendage neogenesis.

candidates.title: Hair follicle micro-particle skin grafting induces scar remodeling via PI3K-AKT signaling: a randomized clinical trial
candidates.timeline: mature scars treated with FUE-derived hair-follicle micro-graft transplantation plus punch excision versus punch excision control; six-month follow-up
candidates.observed: greater scar-volume reduction, lower Vancouver Scar Scale scores and regenerative histologic/transcriptomic changes
candidates.why_not: The regenerative tissue is imported as follicular micrograft material rather than generated de novo from the locked scar.

cross_arm_killer_result.reason: One paper contains an established hypertrophic-scar reversal arm in rabbit and an appendage-return arm in mouse.

next_killer_target: A single arm with pre-treatment histologic/biomechanical documentation of mature scar, intervention only afterward, and lineage/structural evidence that new hair follicles or sebaceous glands formed endogenously within the treated scar.
